mainProgression.description: Sophisticated two-chord vamp using seventh chord voicings that create the smooth, jazzy feel central to the song's character

sectionProgressions.description: Gentle oscillation between tonic major seventh and relative minor seventh creating a contemplative, flowing feel
The same chord movement continues through the chorus with slightly more rhythmic emphasis and dynamic lift
Introduces the IV and V chords for harmonic motion before returning to the main two-chord vamp

harmonicFunction: Emaj7 (Imaj7) - Tonic major seventh providing warm, sophisticated harmonic foundation
C#m7 (vi7) - Relative minor seventh creating smooth, jazzy contrast without tension
Amaj7 (IVmaj7) - Subdominant seventh adding harmonic richness in the bridge
B7 (V7) - Dominant seventh providing gentle resolution back to Emaj7

techniques.name: Jazz/Soul Chord Voicings
techniques.description: Extended chord shapes using major seventh and minor seventh voicings that define the sophisticated harmonic language of Motown soul

notes: Emaj7: 0-2-1-1-0-0 (open voicing with major 7th on G string)
C#m7: X-4-2-4-0-0 or X-4-6-4-5-4 (barre voicing)
Amaj7: X-0-2-1-2-0 (open voicing)
B7: X-2-1-2-0-2 (open voicing)
Keep fingers arched to allow open strings to ring clearly
The seventh intervals add the sophisticated color essential to this song
sequence: Form the Emaj7 shape and strum gently, listening for the major 7th interval
Transition to C#m7 by shifting to the barre position at the 4th fret
Return to Emaj7 with a smooth, unhurried transition
Practice the Amaj7 and B7 shapes separately for the bridge section
Connect all four chords in sequence: Emaj7 - C#m7 - Amaj7 - B7
tips: Practice each seventh chord shape in isolation until it rings cleanly
Listen for the 7th note in each chord - it defines the soul/jazz quality
Use the open string voicings where possible for a richer, more resonant sound
The Emaj7 to C#m7 change should feel effortless - minimize finger movement

techniques.name: Barre Chord Technique
techniques.description: Using barre chord voicings for the C#m7 and bridge chords, requiring clean fretting across multiple strings with the index finger

notes: C#m7 barre chord at 4th fret: X-4-6-4-5-4
Index finger barres across strings at the 4th fret
Ring and pinky fingers handle the 6th and 5th fret notes
Alternative: Use the simplified C#m7 voicing X-4-2-4-0-0
Thumb position behind the neck provides leverage for clean barring
sequence: Position the index finger flat across all strings at the 4th fret
Add the ring finger on the 6th fret of the D string
Add the pinky on the 5th fret of the B string
Strum from the A string down, ensuring every note rings clearly
Release pressure slightly between strums to reduce hand fatigue
tips: Place the index finger close to the fret wire for cleaner barring
Use the edge of the index finger rather than the flat pad for better pressure
If the full barre is too difficult, use the simplified open-string voicing
Build barre chord endurance gradually to avoid hand strain

techniques.name: Smooth Rhythm Comping
techniques.description: Gentle, flowing rhythm guitar pattern with subtle rhythmic variation that supports the vocal and horn arrangements without dominating the mix

notes: Use a relaxed, swinging rhythm feel rather than straight 8th notes
Emphasize beats 2 and 4 with slightly harder strums for soul feel
Add subtle ghost strums (muted) between chord accents for texture
Keep the volume moderate - the guitar sits in the middle of the arrangement
The rhythm should feel like gentle waves, not rigid metronomic hits
sequence: Strum the Emaj7 with a down-up pattern emphasizing the backbeat
Add a light muted strum on the 'and' of beat 1 for rhythmic motion
Accent beat 2 with a slightly fuller strum
Continue the pattern through the chord change to C#m7
Maintain the same rhythmic feel across all sections of the song
tips: Listen to the original recording to internalize the laid-back groove
The guitar should blend with the arrangement, not stand out
Practice with a drum loop or backing track for proper feel
Less is more - restraint creates the sophisticated soul sound

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The intro features overlapping party conversation and conga rhythms with gentle guitar chord stabs establishing the Emaj7 tonality before the full band enters
notes: The guitar enters subtly underneath the spoken conversation
Use very gentle strumming or arpeggiated chord voicings
Let the seventh chord tones ring clearly to establish the harmonic foundation
The mood is warm, intimate, and contemplative from the very start

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse settles into the two-chord Emaj7-C#m7 groove with the guitar providing a supportive rhythmic bed under Marvin Gaye's layered vocal harmonies
notes: The guitar sits back in the mix, supporting the vocal layers
Use a smooth, consistent rhythm without sudden dynamic changes
Let the chord voicings ring and blend with the saxophones and strings
Focus on the backbeat feel (beats 2 and 4) for the soul groove

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus continues the Emaj7-C#m7 movement with slightly increased rhythmic energy and fuller strumming as the vocal melody soars
notes: Add slightly more rhythmic emphasis on the chord accents
The strumming can be a touch fuller but still restrained
Follow the emotional arc of the vocal melody with subtle dynamics
The chorus intensifies the mood without dramatically changing the guitar part

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: The bridge introduces the Amaj7 and B7 chords for harmonic contrast, building tension before gracefully returning to the main Emaj7-C#m7 vamp
notes: The Amaj7 provides a warm subdominant lift away from the main vamp
B7 creates gentle dominant tension that resolves back to Emaj7
Transition smoothly between the bridge chords with no rushed changes
The return to Emaj7-C#m7 should feel like coming home

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The outro rides on the main chord vamp with ad-lib vocals and saxophone, the guitar maintaining its supportive role as the song fades with layered vocal improvisations
notes: Continue the steady rhythm comping pattern through the fade-out
Gradually reduce volume and intensity as the song fades
The guitar remains consistent while other instruments ad-lib over the top
Maintain the groove feel right through to the end of the fade

guitar.recommended: Semi-hollow electric guitar (Gibson ES-335 or Epiphone Sheraton)
alternatives: Any guitar with warm, rounded tone
guitar.pickup: Neck humbucker or P-90 for warm, jazzy tone with smooth high-end rolloff

effects.distortion: None - clean tone is essential for the soul/jazz sound
effects.reverb: Light spring or plate reverb for subtle warmth and space
effects.other: Optional subtle chorus for added thickness; tone knob rolled back to 6-7 on guitar

beginner.focus: Learn the basic Emaj7 and C#m7 chord shapes and simple strumming
steps: Master the open Emaj7 voicing (0-2-1-1-0-0) until it rings cleanly
Learn the simplified C#m7 voicing (X-4-2-4-0-0) or barre version
Practice transitioning between Emaj7 and C#m7 slowly with a metronome
Strum the two-chord vamp with a simple down-up pattern at slow tempo

intermediate.focus: Develop the smooth soul rhythm feel and add bridge section chords
steps: Refine the strumming pattern with backbeat emphasis on beats 2 and 4
Add ghost strums between accented beats for rhythmic texture
Learn the Amaj7 and B7 chord voicings for the bridge section
Play through the full song structure with smooth section transitions

advanced.focus: Add jazz-influenced embellishments and authentic tone reproduction
steps: Explore alternative voicings for Emaj7 and C#m7 up the neck
Add subtle chord melody fills between strums using scale tones
Achieve the warm, round tone with proper amp and guitar settings
Perform with dynamics and musical sensitivity matching the original arrangement

commonMistakes: Using basic major and minor chords instead of the essential seventh voicings
Playing too loudly or forcefully - this song requires restraint and subtlety
Rushing the tempo and losing the relaxed, contemplative groove
Neglecting the smooth quality of chord transitions in favor of speed
practiceRoutine: Warm up with major seventh and minor seventh chord shapes across the neck for 5 minutes
Practice the Emaj7 to C#m7 transition focusing on seamless movement
Work on the backbeat strumming feel with a metronome at 80 BPM
Gradually increase tempo to 98 BPM while maintaining the smooth, jazzy feel
Play along with the original recording focusing on blending with the arrangement
focusAreas: Clean seventh chord voicings with all notes ringing clearly
Smooth, gap-free chord transitions between Emaj7 and C#m7
Backbeat rhythmic feel with subtle dynamic variation
Warm, clean tone appropriate to the soul/jazz genre
metronomeWork: Start at 70 BPM strumming each seventh chord for four beats
Increase to 80 BPM with chord changes every two beats
Add the backbeat accent pattern at 90 BPM
Reach target tempo of 98 BPM with the complete rhythmic feel
